description: Label and group .NET ecosystem updates. The nuget manager already reads global.json, Directory.Build.props and Directory.Packages.props. global.json is the single SDK selector: point mise at it with idiomatic_version_file_enable_tools rather than repeating the version in mise.toml. The custom manager here only exists for repos that still carry that duplicate

customManagers.description: Resolve the dotnet tool in mise config files, for repos that still pin the SDK in both mise.toml and global.json. The mise manager extracts the entry but has no datasource for it and skips it as unsupported-datasource, so that pin never moves and silently drifts. The real fix is to delete the mise entry and add [settings] idiomatic_version_file_enable_tools = ["dotnet"] to mise.toml, which makes mise read global.json itself and leaves one selector that cannot drift. depName matches what the nuget manager emits for global.json, so until then one rule keeps both files in step

packageRules.description: Label all .NET updates. Matches the category rather than the nuget manager alone, so cake and unity3d are covered too
Additionally label NuGet packages, which are the bulk of .NET updates
Group non-major .NET updates into a single PR

Runtime-aligned packages ship in lockstep with the .NET major, so mixing majors across them breaks the build. Group them together including majors, and keep this rule after the general group so it wins

Grpc.Tools generates the C# from the protos at build time, and the Grpc.* and Google.Protobuf packages are the runtime that generated code calls into. They move on one release train, so a major that advanced the generator while leaving the runtime behind would otherwise arrive as two separate PRs. Group them, majors included, the same pairing buf-config makes between a Buf plugin and its runtime. A group holding a major still does not automerge: a branch automerges only if every update in it would, and majors are not automerged, so this is insurance against a split rather than a route to unattended majors
prBodyNotes: If this repo has a `buf.gen.yaml`, move `buf.build/protocolbuffers/csharp` and `buf.build/grpc/csharp` to the releases matching these versions. Renovate cannot read that file, so nothing else will remind you.

packageRules.description: The SDK selector, kept out of the package groups and given a versioning that matches how .NET actually ships. global.json sets the oldest SDK every machine and build agent must already have, because rollForward defaults to patch, which takes the exact version when it is installed and the newest patch in the same feature band when it is not, and the feature band is the real compatibility boundary: Microsoft keys the minimum Visual Studio version to it, so 10.0.1xx is the last band that runs on VS 17.14 while 10.0.2xx and later need VS 18.0. Stock semver reads 10.0.100 to 10.0.404 as a patch, which is how a band change merges unattended and breaks a build that drives MSBuild from Visual Studio. The regex versioning here makes the band the minor instead, so a move inside a band stays a patch and a band change reads as a minor that the hold rule in default.json keeps off automerge. Matching packageName and not depName covers both spellings, since global.json emits depName dotnet-sdk while a mise.toml pin would emit dotnet with packageName dotnet-sdk. Keep this rule after the package groups so the selector leaves them
prBodyNotes: `global.json` sets the **minimum** SDK, not an exact one, because `rollForward` defaults to `patch`, which takes the exact version when it is installed and the newest patch in the same feature band when it is not. Merging this raises the floor for every machine and build agent that builds this repository.

If this repository builds through MSBuild or Visual Studio instead of the `dotnet` CLI, which means `VSBuild@1`, `MSBuild@1`, or a `NuGetCommand@2` restore on a Windows agent, then the SDK feature band has a minimum Visual Studio version that Renovate cannot see. `10.0.1xx` is the last band that runs on VS 17.14, and `10.0.2xx` and later need VS 18.0. Overshooting it fails at restore with `Could not resolve SDK "Microsoft.NET.Sdk"`. Either move the build to `DotNetCoreCLI@2`, so the SDK brings its own MSBuild and the agent's Visual Studio stops mattering, or cap the band in this repository with `allowedVersions`.

packageRules.description: MSBuild SDKs in global.json are build infrastructure, so keep them out of the package groups too
